prompt: Why is clicking through the running app a weak way to check a component?

choices.text: The app is slower than Storybook
choices.why: Speed is not the problem.
Right: you see what the data holds that day; the rest exist only when data and settings line up.

choices.text: Components cannot be inspected inside an app
choices.why: They can; the issue is which states you reach.

choices.text: The app has no dark theme
choices.why: It has one since lesson 5.

prompt: Which of these does Storybook give a design system? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A frame per story, without the app around it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Docs drawn from the stories and comments
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A replacement for the app's own build
choices.why: It is a second site beside the app.

choices.text: A static build that deploys like the planner
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Which way does the dependency between `view.ts` and `components.ts` run?

choices.why: Right: the page uses the library, never the reverse.
Then the library could not be shown without the page.
A cycle would tie them together for good.
`view.ts` imports three components directly.

prompt: Which new state did `weekSummary` gain while its stories were written?

choices.why: It has none.
Not in this lesson.
Right: *Nothing planned this week*.

choices.text: A week in another time zone
choices.why: Weeks are computed in UTC.

prompt: A React project wants the same setup. Which package changes?

choices.why: The program is the same.
Addons work across frameworks.
Right: React installs its own framework package.
The framework package is framework-specific.

prompt: What does `core: { disableTelemetry: true }` do?

choices.text: Stops Storybook reporting errors to the console
choices.why: Console output is unaffected.

choices.text: No usage data leaves for its makers
choices.why: Right; it is on by default.
That panel comes from the addon.
It has nothing to do with reloading.

prompt: Storybook's build goes to the folder `storybook-___`, which is added to `.gitignore`.
In Component Story Format, what is each named export of a stories file?

choices.why: The component is described by the default export.
Right: one state.
Stories become tests only when a runner visits them.
Docs pages are generated per component.

prompt: Pressing *Mark done* in the `ToDo` story does not change the row. Why is that correct?

choices.why: The click happens; it is recorded.

choices.text: The story has a bug the next section fixes
choices.why: It is the intended behaviour.
It runs the component's code.

choices.text: The story holds no state; it logs the call
choices.why: Right: the Actions panel shows `onDone` called with 6.

prompt: You rename the export `Done` to `Finished`. What breaks?

choices.why: Ids are made from the names.
Right: `planner-session-row--done` changes with the name, and tests or bookmarks using it break.
The component does not know its stories.

choices.text: The build, which needs the old name
choices.why: The build succeeds with the new name.

prompt: How many stories, not counting docs pages, did `index.json` list after the second stories file?
What did the `Empty` story reveal about the week summary?

choices.why: It worked; it read badly.

choices.text: It read like a malfunction at zero
choices.why: Right: *0 min planned, 0 min done*.
Themes were not the issue.

choices.text: It counted sessions from other weeks
choices.why: The total is tested in lesson 3.

prompt: You find with Controls that 600 minutes reads well. What should happen to that state?

choices.why: A control's value is gone when the tab closes.
A wiki goes stale and is never tested.
Right: then it is reviewed and tested.
The app's data is not the place for examples.

prompt: What does the decorator in `preview.ts` do before each story draws?

choices.why: There is one stylesheet; the tokens change.

choices.text: Passes the theme to the component
choices.why: The component never learns the theme.
Right; `tokens.css` does the rest.

choices.text: Inverts the colours of the frame
choices.why: Inverting would break the measured contrast.

prompt: The address that shows the `ToDo` story alone, dark, ends in `&globals=___:dark`.
Where does the description on the session row's Docs page come from?

choices.text: A wiki page linked from Storybook
choices.why: Nothing links to a wiki.
The title places it in the sidebar.
There is no such file.
Right.

prompt: An MDX page says *the accent is green*. What is wrong with it?

choices.text: It restates a value that will change
choices.why: Right: embed the value from the tokens instead.
It can embed anything.

choices.text: Docs must be generated, never written
choices.why: Reasons belong in prose.
Designers and testers read them too.

prompt: How do you deploy the built Storybook on a host from lesson 1?

choices.text: It needs a Node server, so it cannot be static
choices.why: The build is a folder of static files.
Right: build command `npm run build-storybook`, output folder `storybook-static`.
It is its own site.
Any static host serves it.

prompt: The `/*` rewrite came along in Storybook's `_redirects`. Why does it not break Storybook's own pages?

choices.why: The file is in the listing.

choices.text: Rewrites only apply to the planner's domain
choices.why: Rules apply to whatever site serves the file.
Right: its pages are files, so nothing asks for a path that is not one.
A page cannot disable a host's rules.

prompt: Put the steps of one test in the order they run.
items: Start the built Storybook on port 6007
Open the story's frame in a theme
Compare a screenshot with the approved one

prompt: The very first `npx playwright test` reports ten failures. What does that mean?

choices.why: Nothing was compared yet.
Right: it wrote them; look at them, and the next run compares.
Then it would not have run at all.
Axe runs after the picture, which failed first.

prompt: How many tests do five stories in two themes make?
Why is the Vitest script changed to `vitest run src`?

choices.text: To make the unit tests faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.
Stories end in `.stories.ts`, which Vitest ignores.
It reads it anywhere.

choices.text: So it does not run the Playwright test as its own
choices.why: Right: both look for `.spec.ts`.

prompt: A lighter grey passed the screenshot test. Why?

choices.text: Screenshots are taken before CSS loads
choices.why: The picture includes the styles.

choices.text: The comparison tolerates small colour differences
choices.why: Right, so that anti-aliasing does not fail every run.

choices.text: Axe ran first and fixed it
choices.why: Axe never changes anything.

choices.text: The `done` story was not in the list
choices.why: It is in the list.

prompt: A teammate on a Mac runs the tests and gets new pictures written. Why?

choices.why: They can.

choices.text: The pictures were deleted by git
choices.why: They are committed.
Right: pictures are named per platform; one machine should be the photographer.

choices.text: The Mac uses a dark theme
choices.why: The theme is set by the test.

prompt: Which of these can neither the screenshot nor axe tell you? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Whether *Mark done* are the right words
choices.why: Right: that is judgement.

choices.text: Whether a pair of colours reaches AA
choices.why: Axe measures that.

choices.text: Whether a picture approved long ago was right
choices.why: Right: it passes forever.
The screenshot caught that.

prompt: A pull request changes `--space-1` and every story's picture fails. What should the reviewer look at first?

choices.text: The axe results, since they are stricter
choices.why: Axe says nothing about spacing.
Right: they show whether the change is wanted; if it is, the updated pictures go in the pull request.

choices.text: The test code, which must be wrong
choices.why: The test did its job: something changed.
A real change fails every time.
